title: Cab booking system design
idea: A cab booking design matches a ride request to one free driver, then drives the trip through a strict lifecycle while a swappable rule prices it.
points: Core entities: `Rider`, `Driver`, `Location`, `Trip`, plus a `TripService` that coordinates them.
A `DriverMatcher` strategy picks the driver: nearest today, top rated tomorrow.
Assigning a driver is an atomic check-and-set, so two trips never share one.
A `TripStatus` enum owns the legal moves; a `FareRule` prices the finished trip.

messages.label: requestRide(pickup)
messages.note: The rider sends a pickup point. A `Trip` is created in state `REQUESTED`.

messages.label: match(pickup, drivers)
messages.note: The service asks the strategy. It never knows which rule is plugged in.

messages.label: D2
messages.note: The matcher filters out busy drivers, then ranks the rest by its own rule.

messages.label: tryAssign()
messages.note: One atomic step marks the driver busy. A second claim gets `false`.

messages.label: true
messages.note: Assigned. The trip moves to `ACCEPTED`; on `false` the service asks the matcher again.

messages.label: start, complete
messages.note: Each move is checked by `TripStatus.canMoveTo`. Skipping a state throws.

messages.label: fare
messages.note: The trip's `FareRule` prices distance and time. Surge wraps the standard rule.

code.title: Matching a driver
code.caption: Two matching strategies over the same drivers, and an assignment that cannot happen twice.

walk.text: `Location` is a value object. Manhattan distance keeps the maths in whole numbers.
`compareAndSet` claims the driver in one step. A real `Driver` entity would be a class, not a record.
`DriverMatcher` is the strategy. `NearestMatcher` skips busy drivers, then takes the closest.
A second rule needs no new class: the interface has one method, so a lambda fits.
D2 is claimed once; the second claim fails, and matching moves on to the next nearest.

code.title: Trip lifecycle and fare
code.caption: The enum decides which moves are legal. The fare rule is injected, so surge is a wrapper.

walk.text: Each state lists where it may go next. Finished trips go nowhere.
`moveTo` refuses an illegal move before it changes anything.
`SurgeFare` wraps any `FareRule` and multiplies its result: a small Decorator.
A started trip cannot be cancelled, so that call throws; completing it is fine.

pitfalls: Do not read `isFree()` then set busy in two steps; claim the driver atomically.
Keep money in whole units such as `long` paise or cents, never `double`.
Avoid `if (status == ...)` checks scattered across services; let the enum own the transitions.

quiz.q: What is the first line `TripDemo` prints?
quiz.why: The trip is `STARTED`, and `STARTED` may only move to `COMPLETED`. `moveTo` throws with the current and requested states.

takeaway: Match with a strategy, assign atomically, let the status enum guard every move.

starters: How would I find nearby drivers fast when there are thousands of them?
What should happen if the assigned driver never accepts the ride?
Should cancellation fees live in Trip or in a separate class?
